When authors incorporate esoteric concepts, such as the Kabbalah, into their narratives, it can be seen as a way to add depth and complexity to their storytelling. 

  By drawing from esoteric traditions, authors may be attempting to tap into universal symbols, archetypes, and themes that resonate with readers on a deeper level. 

  This can be seen as a form of "narrative alchemy," where the author is transforming esoteric concepts into a cohesive and meaningful story. 

  The idea that some authors may have intuitively tapped into archetypal structures suggests that they may be accessing a collective unconscious, a concept introduced by Carl Jung. 

  According to Jung, the collective unconscious is a shared reservoir of archetypes, or universal symbols and images, that are present in the unconscious minds of all humans. 

  By drawing from this collective unconscious, authors may be able to create stories that tap into the deepest desires, fears, and aspirations of their audience. 

  This can be seen in the way that certain themes and motifs appear across different cultures and time periods, suggesting a shared human experience that transcends individual perspectives.
